_comment: Flags exports a branch ADDS whose reference count across src/ is 1 — the declaration
alone. That is the 'built, tested, never wired' class: a symbol shipped by a wave that no
production path calls, green the whole way because every assertion pointed at the
WHY A DELTA AND NOT A CENSUS — the settled empirical negative, recorded so nobody
re-litigates it. Measured on src/lib/** at e8a9c05: 1,812 exports, 971 with zero
non-owning-file consumers — 475 runtime symbols WITH a test consumer, 350 type-only, 146
with no consumer anywhere. A whole-repo guard would demand ~971 allowlist rows, and the
475 bucket is CLAUDE.md's own MANDATED test-importable-seam pattern, so the guard would
fight the house style and be allowlisted into uselessness on day one. The same measurement
on the wave that shipped the defect: 23 new exports, 2 flagged — hoursUntilUtcDayReset (the
real defect) and dailyUsedFor (a second of the same class). Two rows per wave, not 971.
EXEMPT BY CONSTRUCTION, never by row:
· type-only exports (`export type` / `export interface`) — a type has no call site
· re-exports (`export { x } from` / `export * from`) — they declare nothing new
Both are handled in code, so no one can be tempted to allowlist an entire class.

_why: REPORT-first per house law (G-D). Both conditions must hold to flip to block: zero
unexplained hits AND the date passed. A numeric criterion alone can never fire if the
count does not heal; a date alone flips a guard that is still noisy.
not_before is +7d rather than the usual +14d because the measured signal is 2 flagged
out of 23 new exports on a real wave — a rate that does not need a fortnight of
observation to judge. Every run appends its count to the ledger, so the flip decision
reads a series rather than a guess.
PROMOTED 2026-08-31 by OPS-DARK-ARTIFACT-GATE-PROMOTE-W1 R2. mode is now `block`, and it
is the ONLY thing the script reads — the old auto-promotion arm was UNREACHABLE CODE and
has been deleted rather than fixed. It read `dark.length <= max_unexplained` at a point
the script only reaches when `dark.length >= 1`, against `max_unexplained: 0`, so it could
never be true; the date leg had passed since 2026-08-16 and made no difference. A criterion
that cannot fire is not a criterion, and leaving it in place would have kept this guard
permanently in report — the `decoration` shape the git rules already name.
The fields below are RETAINED, not vestigial: they are the promotion RECORD, and
tests/unit/promotion-independence.test.ts asserts every promotion block carries an
instrument. Neither is read by the gate any more.
The flip was gated on a REPAIR, not on the clock. As shipped the detector measured 33 false
positives and 5 false negatives against the TypeScript compiler's own scanner over 1,847
export declarations at d26898cf — 16.1% of the unexempt flagged set. After R1.5 it measures
FP=0 / FN=0. Blast radius at flip time was measured, not assumed: of 103 worktrees, 10 were
unlanded, 9 of those lack the script entirely (they skip loudly) and the 10th returns PASS.

instrument.population: Dark exports in TRACKED SOURCE, per run — the unexplained exported symbols themselves, not the log rows that record how many there were.
instrument.rederive: Re-run `node scripts/check-new-dark-exports.mjs` at any commit. The dark-export set is derived from tracked source — exported symbols resolved against their consumers — so the count for any commit is recomputable from the tree alone. `.git/algovault-dark-exports.log` is the CACHE of that series, never the population: deleting it would lose the history but not a single fact about any commit.
instrument.reason: B, not A: the gate writes the ledger the flip decision reads. B, not C: the number is a property of tracked source, so a deliberate run recomputes whatever the tree already contains and cannot manufacture an unexplained export without someone first committing one. Added by OPS-PROMOTION-INSTRUMENT-INDEPENDENCE-W1 CH1 — this block was one of THREE promotion criteria that wave's own spec did not know existed, found only because R1.4 discovers the set by scanning ops/*.json instead of trusting a list.

name_exemptions.reason: Module-level cache/state reset seams. CLAUDE.md MANDATES them ('Module-level singleton caches need full reset + per-cache partial + read-only inspector'), they exist to be called from tests, and the leading underscore already marks them as non-API. Measured on the reference wave: 2 of the 23 new exports.

Same class, older naming (`_resetBinanceAdapterCaches`, `_setSnapshotForTest` siblings). Kept as a separate pattern rather than widened into the one above so a future rename does not silently exempt more than intended.

symbol_exemptions.reason: OPS-QUOTA-METER-SURFACE-CONFORMANCE-W1 CH1. The quota-surface conformance registry is CI-FACING BY DESIGN: its consumers are scripts/check-quota-surface-conformance.mjs (through dist/) and tests/unit/quota-surface-conformance.test.ts. Zero src/ consumers is the INTENDED end state rather than a wiring gap — a build-time contract that src/ imported would become a runtime dependency. This is an explanation, not a suppression: the row is still printed and counted as `exempt` on every run, and only `dark` scores the promotion criterion.

OPS-QUOTA-METER-SURFACE-CONFORMANCE-W1 CH1. The sentence every quota surface is judged against, held in code rather than in a wave document precisely so a later reader cannot widen it in prose. Asserted by tests/unit/quota-surface-conformance.test.ts; no src/ consumer by design, same rationale as QUOTA_SURFACES.

GEO-ROBOTS-CONTENT-SIGNAL-W1 R2. The AI-crawler allowlist is an OPS-FACING policy SoT: its consumers are scripts/check-robots-ai-allowlist.mjs (which reads this file's array literal directly, because the gate runs on a host with node 20 and no build step) and tests/unit/robots-ai-allowlist.test.ts, which asserts that reader's output EQUALS this constant so the two cannot drift. Zero src/ consumers is the INTENDED end state, not a wiring gap - the list governs a static file served by Caddy and an edge policy surface, neither of which the runtime ever touches, and importing it into src/ would turn a build-time contract into a runtime dependency. Same rationale as QUOTA_SURFACES. An explanation, not a suppression: the row is still printed and counted as `exempt` on every run.

GEO-WELLKNOWN-DISCOVERY-W1 R2. Same class and same rationale as AI_CRAWLER_ALLOWLIST directly above: this is an OPS-FACING discovery-policy SoT whose consumers are scripts/generate-wellknown.mjs (which EMITS the /.well-known/ documents from it) and scripts/check-robots-ai-allowlist.mjs (which PROBES them), plus tests/unit/robots-ai-allowlist.test.ts asserting the text reader's output EQUALS this constant so the two cannot drift. Both scripts run on the deploy host, whose node is 20 with no TypeScript loader and whose dist/ is a stale April artifact, so they read this file's literal as TEXT rather than importing it. Zero src/ consumers is the INTENDED end state: these govern static documents served by Caddy and a response-header policy surface, neither of which the runtime ever touches. Importing it into src/ would turn a build-time document contract into a runtime dependency for no gain.
